name: gamescom 2026

days.label: Wednesday
days.note: Public entry only with the €65.50 Wildcard ticket (from 13:00) — the quietest way to play popular demos before the weekend crush.

days.label: Thursday
days.note: Best full public day for hands-on demos — noticeably calmer than Fri–Sat.

days.label: Friday
days.note: Fills up over the day; mornings still workable for big booths. gamescom GDQ speedrun showcase starts (Congress Center North).

days.label: Saturday
days.note: Busiest and most expensive day, usually sells out — avoid for hands-on play if you can. City Festival in the evening.

days.label: Sunday
days.note: Most relaxed public day; booths start winding down late afternoon. Free entry possible via completed gamescom epix quests.

onl.note: Hosted by Geoff Keighley, ~2 h show. Free stream on YouTube, Twitch and Steam. In-person tickets (€34.50) sold out.

tickets: Online-only via the official gamescom shop — no on-site box office. Day tickets: Thu/Fri/Sun €31.50 (discounted €22.50), Saturday €41.00; evening tickets from 16:00 €10.50–13.00; family ticket €69.50–86.00; Wednesday Wildcard €65.50. Opening Night Live tickets are sold out; Saturday historically sells out before the show. Day tickets include free VRS public transport in the Cologne region.

areas.name: Entertainment area
areas.description: The consumer show: big publisher booths, playable demos, stages, giveaways.

areas.name: Business area
areas.description: Trade & media only (Wed–Fri), West Entrance; closed Sat/Sun.

areas.name: Event Arena
areas.description: Big stage shows, concerts and esports (incl. Prime League offline finals).

areas.name: Cosplay Village
areas.description: Cosplay contest, photo booths, workshops and the Artist Area.

areas.name: Merchandise Area
areas.description: The only area where exhibitors may sell goods — main merch shopping halls.

areas.name: Cards & Boards Area
areas.description: Card and board game communities and vendors.

areas.name: Indie Area / Indie Arena Booth
areas.description: ~200 indie games from 182 developers — see the Indie Arena Booth exhibitor entry.

areas.name: Retro & Family Area
areas.description: 50 years of gaming history plus family-friendly games.

areas.name: Signing Area
areas.description: Content creator autograph and meet-and-greet sessions.

areas.name: gamescom epix
areas.description: Free digital quest program (7 story chapters, started Aug 3) — on-site booth quests, collector cards, and free Sunday tickets for completing all chapters.

areas.name: gamescom GDQ
areas.description: New Games Done Quick speedrunning charity showcase, Aug 28–30, Congress Center North.

areas.name: City Festival
areas.description: Free open-air concerts and gaming zones in Cologne's city center (Ringe), Aug 29–30 evenings.

crowdTips: Saturday is the busiest, priciest day and usually sells out — do hands-on play Thursday or Sunday instead.
Wednesday with a Wildcard ticket (entry from 13:00) is the quietest way to play the hottest demos.
Arrive well before doors open and pick the entrance nearest your first must-play booth — big booths build 2–4 h queues within the first hour.
Pick 5–10 must-play booths in advance (official gamescom app + hall plan) and hit your single most-wanted booth right at opening.
Some large booths hand out time slots or fast-lane wristbands in the morning via their own apps — check exhibitors' socials the week before.
Take the train/tram to Koeln Messe/Deutz — day tickets include free VRS public transport; don't drive.
Evening tickets (from 16:00, €10.50–13) are a cheap second visit; queues shrink in the last 2–3 hours.
Do gamescom epix quests — completing all chapters can earn a free Sunday ticket.
